title: Kenya Health Ministry coordinates US$80M maternal health investment with Beginnings Fund in Nairobi
summary: The meeting, led by Beginnings Fund Chief Executive Officer Alice Kangethe, focused on implementation arrangements and coordination between the fund and the Ministry of Health.
thbAction: Map the news to THB's provider CRM for referral growth, patient lifecycle engagement, and multi-facility relationship management across hospital and provider networks.
contentHtml:
KENYA—Principal Secretary for Medical Services Dr. Ouma Oluga met the Beginnings Fund team at Afya House in Nairobi to coordinate implementation of an US$80 million, five-year investment plan aimed at reducing preventable maternal and newborn deaths and stillbirths.

The meeting, led by Beginnings Fund Chief Executive Officer Alice Kangethe, focused on implementation arrangements and coordination between the fund and the Ministry of Health.

Dr. David Gathara and Dr. Gladwel Gatheca also attended, representing the ministry’s Director of Family Health.

Investment targets high-burden counties and health facilities

Co-designed with the Kenyan government, the investment plan will cover 21 counties with a high burden of maternal and newborn deaths and 200 priority health facilities.

These include 20 Level 5 hospitals, 136 Level 4 hospitals and 44 high-volume health centres.

The programme complements the government’s Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) Investment Case and the Every Woman Every Newborn Everywhere (EWENE) Acceleration Plan.

Its implementation will focus on improving access to essential services, strengthening health systems and addressing gaps in the quality of care during pregnancy, childbirth and the newborn period.

Funding to strengthen maternal and newborn care

The investment will support emergency obstetric and newborn care, improve access to essential medical supplies and technologies, and strengthen training and support for healthcare workers.

 It will also target weaknesses in referral systems, blood availability and maternity and newborn care infrastructure.

In addition, the programme will integrate maternal and newborn health data into the TaifaCare platform to improve performance monitoring and accountability.

Better access to reliable health data can help county health departments and facilities track service delivery, identify gaps and allocate resources according to local needs.

Joint governance and sustainable financing

The Ministry of Health and Beginnings Fund will establish joint governance arrangements to oversee implementation, with Dr. Oluga designated to co-chair the Steering Committee.

The framework will set out institutional responsibilities, measurable milestones and performance-based financing mechanisms, alongside county participation and progressive domestic financing.

These arrangements are intended to strengthen coordination between national and county governments, link funding to measurable service improvements and support the continuation of essential maternal and newborn health services after the five-year investment period.

By 2030, the plan is expected to reach 5.9 million mothers and newborns with higher-quality care and prevent an estimated 46,494 maternal and newborn deaths and stillbirths.
